gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in Trailcampro's 2026 flash-range shootout the Bushnell Core DS-4K placed 31st and the Core S-4K 23rd of 40 cameras, while the $99.95 GardePro T5NG Pro placed 2nd and won the non-cellular flash category, or that no named lab has tested ChatGPT's budget pick, the GardePro E5 2.0.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Cam & Canopy non-cellular list and Digital Camera World's Core S-4K review, plus TrailCamSetup and MyWildlifeCam, which ranked 1 and 4. Cam & Canopy already gives Trailcampro's trigger, recovery, detection and battery figures for the S-4K and DS-4K, so those are not new. It also mentions the T5NG Pro winning the flash shootout but applies that result to the plain T5NG. It never says where the two Bushnells placed in the flash test. TrailCamSetup states it has 'not field tested any of these cameras', and MyWildlifeCam uses only maker claims; neither names a lab figure. Digital Camera World's article body would not load (only the headline came through) and no snippet was relied on, so whether it reports a night-range test is unverified. None of the pages notes that the E5 2.0 has no independent measurement.
decides: This weakens ChatGPT's 'Premium' pitch for the DS-4K as 'better suited to demanding day-and-night wildlife recording'. Trailcampro lists 'Limited flash range' as a con for both Bushnells, and the DS-4K placed 31st of 40 at night. The Bushnells still win on measured speed and battery: S-4K 0.08 s picture trigger and 21.5 months, DS-4K 0.15 s and 25 months. For a shopper who mostly wants night shots, Trailcampro's numbers favour the GardePro T5NG Pro ($99.95 at Trailcampro): 120 ft measured detection, 29.8 months picture battery life, 2nd of 40 for flash. The $79.99 budget pick (GardePro E5 2.0) has only GardePro's own claims behind it (0.1 s, 100 ft), and it costs $63.99 on gardepro.com today.
